title: Case G — flow behind a tree belt
summary: Field observation behind the Tsuiji-matsu tree belt (a porous windbreak, 74 m × 2 m × 7 m with a 1.2 m gap below): normalised mean speed and k at 28 points on the centre section (sonic anemometers).

configuration.belt: Tsuiji-matsu (Japanese black pine), trimmed to a rectangle; 74 m long (y), 2 m deep (x), 7 m tall, 1.2 m bottom gap; shading rate 81 % after pruning (data paper section 3.7)
configuration.location: Taisha-machi, Hikawa-gun, Shimane, Japan; west end of an elementary-school playground
configuration.instrument: 3-D ultrasonic anemometers (KAIJO DA-600 with TR-90Tx) at four heights on a movable tower, 5 Hz, 10 min or more per line (26 Dec 2000); approach flow 120 min (28 Dec 2000) at 1.5, 3, 6, 9 m
configuration.normalisation: velocity_ratio = U/UH and k_ratio = k/UH^2, UH = the mean wind speed at 7 m during each measurement period (interpolated with the approach flow's power law, index 0.22); nothing is published in m/s
configuration.approach_flow_normalisation: AF_caseG.csv is U/Ub and k/Ub^2 with Ub = U at 9 m; divide by UH/Ub = 0.946 (power law 0.22) for the table's normalisation
configuration.scale_note: full scale: a field observation, there is no model

frame.origin: the leeward face of the tree belt at ground level, on the vertical section through the belt's centre
frame.x: +x downwind: the belt occupies x in [-2, 0] m, the measurement lines lie behind it at x = 1.75 ... 35 m
frame.y: +y along the belt (y in [-37, 37] m); every point is on y = 0
frame.z: +z up; the belt spans z in [1.2, 7] m; points at z = 1.5, 3, 4.5, 6 m
frame.wind_direction_rotation: one direction, toward +x (perpendicular to the belt); the field wind's angle to the belt normal is not published

inflow_fit.method: power law on the four published heights (1.5, 3, 6, 9 m) of U/Ub; the readme states the index 0.22
inflow_fit.note: derived during cleaning, not published as a fit; the profile carries 2 decimals, so the fitted index is good to about +/-0.01

units.U: dimensionless, U/Ub (Ub = mean speed at 9 m, not published in m/s)
dimensionless, U/Ub (Ub = mean speed at 9 m, not published in m/s)

fit.method: power law on the four published heights (1.5, 3, 6, 9 m) of U/Ub; the readme states the index 0.22
fit.note: derived during cleaning, not published as a fit; the profile carries 2 decimals, so the fitted index is good to about +/-0.01

benchmark_data.note: the measured profile and the fit of it are the benchmark's data as cleaned here; everything under `recommended` is a choice

recommended.status: RECOMMENDED by this repository (not part of the benchmark): no log law fits this case (inflow_fit says why); use the measured approach-flow profile as a tabulated inlet (approach_flow.csv). Any inlet may be submitted; say which in submission.yaml
recommended.profile: U(z) and, where published, k(z) tabulated from approach_flow.csv; epsilon = Cmu^0.5 k dU/dz where k is published, else from your own closure
recommended.openfoam: fixedProfile (OpenFOAM.org) with the table, or timeVaryingMappedFixedValue: cases/{id}/inflow_openfoam.txt holds the table

flow_direction.meaning: +x is along the wind at WD = 0: flowDir (1 0 0); another WD rotates it about +z by the case's rotation sense (frame.wind_direction_rotation)

inflow.domain: the extents, blockage and cell sizes of Eddy3D's domains are not in its snapshots and are not stated here; mesh.cells and the scale are, where the snapshot has them

probes.columns_meaning: the key columns of a scored file (point_id with config, campaign, instrument, run and wind_direction_deg as the case has them), x, y, z in m (case frame), and scored_as: the families the row is scored in (vector, k, thermistor_bracket, concentration, theta, joined by +)

scoring.U_ref_meaning: the table holds U/U_H and k/U_H^2 with U_H the wind at the tree height (7 m); give ratios over your own U(7 m) upwind

scored_as.vector: U, V, W and the speed |U| against the split-fibre, LDV or hot-wire components (velocity.U, velocity.V, velocity.W, speed)
scored_as.thermistor_bracket: a mean scalar speed (thermistor, cup or sonic anemometer) against |U| (vs.vector) and sqrt(|U|^2 + 2k) (vs.scalar)

scoring.conventions: velocities and the speed over U_ref, k over U_ref^2 (Cases E, F and G publish ratios already); U, V, W, |U| and the thermistor bracket scored as signed velocities (FAC2's ratio keeps the sign; hit rate D = 0.25, W = 0.05); k by the plain definitions (D = 0.25 only); a thermistor, cup or sonic reading (a mean scalar speed) scored against |U| (vs.vector) and sqrt(|U|^2 + 2k) (vs.scalar), the two ends of its bracket; c* = C/c0 with one detection limit per case, 1e-3 of the largest measured value; theta = (T_floor - T)/(T_floor - T_H) scored like a positive velocity. The same conventions score the served Eddy3D results (docs/validation/method.md).
scoring.tool: python validation/score_submissions.py <folder>, from a checkout of the repository (requirements.txt)

metric_meaning.MeanObserved: mean of the measured, normalised quantity
metric_meaning.MeanPredicted: mean of the modelled, normalised quantity
metric_meaning.Fb: fractional bias, 2 (mean_obs - mean_pred) / (mean_obs + mean_pred); positive = model low
metric_meaning.Fac2: fraction of points within a factor of two (harsh near zero for sign-changing V and W)
metric_meaning.HitRate: fraction of points within D = 0.25 relative or W = 0.05 U_H absolute
metric_meaning.GeometricPairs: pairs with both values positive (used for Mg/Vg)
metric_meaning.null: a metric that is undefined for the data (for example Mg and Vg when no pair has both values positive; Fb, Nmse and Nad of a signed velocity component of Case H or I whose observed and predicted means are not both positive)

known_issues: FIELD data: full-scale metres, no model, and nothing in m/s. The table carries U/UH (velocity_ratio) and k/UH^2 (k_ratio), UH = the mean speed at 7 m during each period; the approach-flow table carries U/Ub and k/Ub^2 (Ub = U at 9 m) in its U and k columns, which are dimensionless here.
The readme lists the heights of the lee measurement as 1.5, 3.0, 6.0, 9.0 m; the table, the workbook, the drawing and the data paper have 1.5, 3, 4.5, 6 m.
The tree belt is a porous canopy (shading rate 81 % after pruning): the served geometry is its 2 m × 74 m × 7 m envelope with the 1.2 m gap, and a solver needs a canopy (drag) model.

The approach profile (28 Dec 2000, 120 min) and the lee measurements (26 Dec 2000, 10 min or more) are from different days. Behind the belt k/UH^2 is 0.040-0.072 at 5 H, 3-8 times below the approach flow's 0.26-0.31 at the same heights; the files do not say why.
Only 28 numbers per quantity exist, on one centre section, one time-average each, with no repeats and no uncertainty.
The wind direction relative to the belt normal during the measurement is not published; the case is two-dimensional by assumption.
